sources_considered.why: Primary research estimates the finite supply of usable human-generated public text and explains the forecast's limits.
Independent evaluation compares reasoning models using the same testing framework and reports the additional time required.
Primary developer results compare reasoning capabilities across mathematics, science and coding.
Independent autonomy evaluations supply material qualifications: improvements were not uniform across tasks.
Read Epoch's independent GPQA comparison, but the retrieved page gives only a relative publication age. Other dated sources were sufficient.

evidence_items.explanation: The estimate supports an approaching constraint on usable human-generated public text under continuing scaling trends. It does not show that data was already exhausted, and the discussion identifies other data sources and ways progress could continue.

Using its baseline testing framework, ARC Prize reports public-evaluation scores of 21.2% for o1-preview and 9% for GPT-4o. This is post-March capability progress, although the evaluator also reports substantially greater inference time.

evidence_items.locator: Evals; supporting comparisons in Appendix A
evidence_items.explanation: Appendix A reports o1-preview improvements over GPT-4o on mathematics, science and coding, including pass@1 scores of 44.6 versus 9.3 on AIME and 73.3 versus 50.6 on GPQA Diamond. These are developer measurements, but they broaden the evidence beyond a single reasoning benchmark.

METR found limited success on its seven research tasks and no improvement over its best existing model on the autonomy suite. This qualifies the breadth of progress, but METR also warned that its testing could underestimate the models' capabilities.

unresolved_gaps: The data estimate concerns public human-generated text, not all possible training material.
No single evaluation captures every meaning of actual capabilities.
The capability comparisons do not hold inference compute constant.
